truthBoundary: This aggregate reconciles the frozen 2026-08-21 live snapshot, copied source, isolated behavior, current shard artifacts, and explicitly bounded prior evidence. It proves only the named properties at those evidence boundaries; it does not prove universal Cortex health, current or future behavior, scale/endurance beyond exercised checks, or that model/provider work occurred unless a cited receipt establishes it. Shard completion means the audit artifacts are terminal and internally validated, not that product surfaces are green. No live service was accessed, deployed, restarted, written, or externally acted upon during aggregation, and no candidate patch was deployed.
deduplicationRule: Merge only shared causal boundaries; preserve all source IDs, affected surfaces, evidence, limitations, and contrary evidence through contradiction links.

findings.title: Readiness and component status remain false-green under degradation
findings.rootCause: Liveness, structural presence, dependency behavior, and progress are conflated; failures are caught or displayed while success/active/healthy remains literal or independent of the failed component.
symptoms: Frozen ready=true and health=healthy coexist with architect in safeModeSkipped.
Injected oracle import failure and ghost missing router export remained ready=true.
/health says healthy while readiness=false.
Knowledge/L22 say active with null database counts.
A corrupt watchdog database is converted to zero and healthy.
HUD may inject success=true into successful dictionary responses.
Injected failures from semantic and structured stores yielded an active successful response with both counts null.
impact: Operators and callers can receive an unqualified green signal while API components are absent or failed.
Routing, monitors, and operators can send memory traffic to an unavailable level and misdiagnose data loss as healthy operation.
Traffic and operator automation cannot distinguish dependency outage from healthy idle state, preventing timely isolation/recovery and making green claims misleading.

evidence.detail: Missing required routers/paths/graph yielded ready=false/503 but health_status=healthy.
Both database-down status handlers returned success=true/status=active.
Invalid SQLite bytes produced last_reason=healthy and exit 0.
Frozen top-level health/readiness were green, but these checks are structural and point-in-time only.
Failure values do not affect success/status.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: In main.py, separate core readiness from degraded component state; make failed/missing routers part of the declared policy and derive health labels/components from checks rather than literals.
Return per-backend checks and derive active/degraded/failed plus success from required capabilities; add one-backend and both-backend failure regressions.

Separate liveness, structural readiness, and bounded deep health. Return dependency-specific availability/error/staleness, make required dependency loss produce readiness 503, remove generic success injection, and have the watchdog inspect those specific fields.

findings.title: Internal Cortex composition targets an unbound legacy port
findings.rootCause: Internal service addressing is duplicated as port 8888 literals/defaults while the frozen deployment listens on 127.0.0.1:8000.
symptoms: 66 occurrences across 32 runtime files target 8888.
Frozen listening-ports evidence has Cortex only on 127.0.0.1:8000.
Orchestrator workflow steps and Sentinel preflight target 8888.
Nexus kernel/level probes degrade silently.
Aggregate health/readiness can remain green because they do not test self-call reachability.
impact: Cross-level orchestration, monitoring, consistency filters, queue calls, and memory/provider composition can fail or fall back while the service remains traffic-ready.
Status probes and orchestration can silently report unavailable/degraded peers despite the service being present on its configured port.

evidence.detail: Cortex listens on 127.0.0.1:8000; no 8888 listener was captured.
Copied main.py and nexus.py match frozen hashes and byte counts.
Workflow base and Sentinel scan URL use 127.0.0.1:8888.
78 :8888 matches across 38 scoped files, including worker, routers, modules, and historical scripts.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Centralize the internal Cortex base URL (default 8000) and replace self-HTTP calls with in-process dependencies where feasible.

Introduce one CORTEX_INTERNAL_BASE_URL derived from CORTEX_HOST/CORTEX_PORT, migrate current-runtime self-calls, and add a startup/readiness self-reachability probe plus a deployed-port regression. First verify whether any intentionally separate 8888 namespace exists.

findings.title: Canonical level and topology identity is duplicated and stale
findings.rootCause: Level names, ordinals, status paths, aliases, topology totals, and HUD/Nexus maps are independently maintained instead of derived from one registry.
symptoms: L3/L8/L21 names conflict.
L9/L36 share /meta_conductor/status.
L26/L36 share /conductor/status and /orchestrator/status.
L12 canonical /hive/status reports level 3.
Isolated status returned 34 even though the module's fallback set contains 38 entries.
impact: Routing, dashboards, automation, and status consumers can attach the wrong identity or health meaning to a level.
Topology observability and cross-level completeness claims are misleading.

evidence.observation: Stale status reproduced without invoking its write-initializing constructor.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Derive the count/names from the shared live level registry and expose the registry version/source.
Make modules/level_registry.py the only level/name/path source; derive Nexus/HUD/Mirror maps and enforce unique canonical targets plus payload-level identity tests.

findings.title: Audit evidence is byte-valid but not self-contained or directly replayable
findings.rootCause: The checksum manifest and replay instructions retain inaccessible capture paths or missing/currently mismatched entry points instead of a relocatable campaign receipt.
symptoms: Direct sha256sum -c cannot resolve paths in the isolated copy; deterministic prefix rebasing validates all 14 entries.
All hashes match after basename remap but literal sha256sum -c fails all entries.
The documented replay command has no file to execute.
impact: A downstream auditor cannot directly verify or replay the current campaign from the delivered evidence bundle without reconstructing assumptions.
Evidence replay is less portable and can be mistaken for an integrity failure.

evidence.detail: 14/14 data files match after safe remap.
Literal manifest check exits 1 for 14 inaccessible paths.
No run-campaign.sh exists in the copied workspace.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Emit manifest-relative paths and the exact validation command; include a root-relative current-ID replay script, frozen input/config/tool/model hashes, and a verifier matching green/red/partial/not_observable.
Emit snapshot-relative checksum paths at capture time.

findings.title: Oracle defaults to a synthetic done=true completion
findings.rootCause: The emergency bypass defaults on when its environment flag is absent and uses a completed response for an acknowledgement that performed no provider work.
symptoms: The isolated default response used model oracle-emergency-bypass, lane emergency_static, and never called the provider.
Existing integration tests set the bypass false and do not exercise the default.
The response says request accepted but reports completion.
No provider/reasoning receipt is attached.
impact: Callers can accept a static 'request accepted' acknowledgement as finished reasoning or provider compute.
Users and downstream automation can interpret a non-executed request as a completed reasoning result; completion and quality telemetry are polluted.

evidence.observation: done=true static completion reproduced with the provider replaced by a function that would fail if invoked.

evidence.detail: With the variable absent, copied oracle_chat returned model=oracle-emergency-bypass, lane=emergency_static, done=true.
(os.getenv(...) or 'true') selects the branch.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Default fail-closed; require explicit degradation state; return 503 or done=false and first-class origin/providerInvoked/degraded fields.

Default the bypass off, model bypass output as accepted/deferred/degraded with done=false, and require a provider/execution receipt before done=true. Capture the deployed environment value before rollout.
confidence: high for copied default; live setting not observable

findings.title: Worker completion and handoff lack a required result and integrity binding
findings.rootCause: Counter/process booleans can satisfy completion without an ordered usable final result, while result, source/config identity, timestamps, and the handoff digest are not bound together.
symptoms: A no-network fake emitted two counters and one input token; actual launcher returned ok/completion true and handoff complete with summary null/unavailable.
Copied hashes match frozen bytes, yet no committed identity or replayable execution proof is available.
Status complete coexists with remaining work and null completion time.
Changing exit code, usage, and remaining work leaves handoffId unchanged.
impact: A completion claim cannot be traced to a committed implementation/config solely from frozen evidence.
Downstream consumers can confuse process exit with completed objective or treat a stable identifier as an integrity receipt.
Malformed, compromised, or incomplete streams can become successful result/handoff artifacts despite no demonstrated work product.

evidence.command: node --require ./artifacts/persistence-learning-execution/fake-ssh-preload.cjs scripts/codex-worker-launcher.mjs exec --host fake@example --codex-bin /opt/codex --workspace /srv/work --prompt 'isolated fake transport test' --transport-timeout-ms 100 --provider-timeout-ms 100

evidence.result: complete with unavailable summary while canonical review boundary remains false/true

evidence.detail: Counter-only success predicate and optional summary.
Hashes present; launcher/handoff untracked.
Semantic negative harness reproduced all conditions.
Existing 3/3 suite passes but covers bounded extraction/determinism/failure sidecar, not these truth properties.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Use execution_complete_review_required when work remains, validate RFC3339 timestamps/order, include exit/usage/remaining work in identity, and bind the handoff to the exact result artifact SHA-256 plus verifier receipt.

Validate one ordered turn schema/identity, terminal status and absence of error/cancel; require observed requested model plus final agent message or typed result; bind handoff to result digest and fail closed on missing result.
Version execution scripts and record source/config hashes, launcher version, event/result digest, and handoff digest in every result; freeze a sanitized result with future audits.

findings.title: OpenClaw Cortex plugins lack one principal-derivation contract
findings.rootCause: Route and memory integrations use different configured-versus-callback precedence, and configured-user preference can collapse distinct callback principals sharing a session.
symptoms: One synthetic callback produced route principal configured-main/configured-channel and memory principal runtime-child/runtime-channel while user/session matched.
impact: If more than one untrusted sender can share an OpenClaw session, user isolation collapses despite valid HMAC signatures.
Routing, memory, cache, and policy state can be scoped to different principals for the same turn.

evidence.source: route-gate index.ts:1235-1250; cortex-memory-bridge/index.ts:1441-1463; corrected parity harness
evidence.observation: principalParity=false under identical trusted callback data.

evidence.fact: route gate and memory bridge preferConfiguredUserId=true
distinct callback users sharing a session produced the same configured user/session signature and route-state namespace

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Prefer trusted callback sender identity, or enforce and verify a single-principal sender allowlist before assigning the configured deployment principal.
Use one principal derivation helper and one callback-precedence contract with cross-plugin regression fixtures.
findings.evidenceQualification: Security results tied only to missing V-CODEC-HANDLER/V-AUTH-SCOPE/V-EXTERNAL-AST command bodies are treated as Tier D; independent Tier A/B/C evidence is retained and affected coverage rows are downgraded where necessary.

findings.title: Memory principal enforcement is absent from compatibility and Codec routes
findings.rootCause: The authenticated tenant/workspace/session principal is enforced only on canonical receipt/commit paths; compatibility and Codec handlers accept global or caller-selected namespaces.
impact: A caller can read or write memory outside its tenant/workspace/session boundary, potentially exposing client or PHI-bearing content.
Cross-session Codec reads, state poisoning, policy/lineage disclosure, persistence through GET flags, and optional Oracle invocation are possible within reachability of the service.

evidence.fact: KnowledgeSearchRequest and L22StoreRequest expose no scope/HMAC/idempotency fields
knowledge search made identical global calls and L22 store forwarded no scope or idempotency
global robust_search is called without authenticated principal filtering
27 Codec operations are frozen-live; GET operations have no security requirement
wrong-HMAC and identity-free event writes selected victim-session; unauthenticated status read returned it
session_key/query/body/header is trusted and no Codec handler calls principal authentication

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Authenticate every Codec route, derive session solely from the authenticated principal, reject caller mismatches, namespace state by principal, and convert side-effecting GET modes to authenticated POSTs.

Require one shared AuthenticatedMemoryPrincipal dependency on every memory route, derive storage/search namespaces from it, reject body/header mismatches, and bind idempotency to principal plus payload.
findings.evidenceQualification: Security results tied only to missing V-CODEC-HANDLER/V-AUTH-SCOPE/V-EXTERNAL-AST command bodies are treated as Tier D; independent Tier A/B/C evidence is retained and affected coverage rows are downgraded where necessary.

findings.title: Loopback and a shared bearer token are treated as principal authority
findings.rootCause: The global write gate admits tokenless loopback and derives no principal, tenant, session, target, or action capability; the browser bridge relies on that bypass.
impact: Any process able to reach the loopback listener receives the same write authority, including host, network, device, scheduler, and memory actions.
The enabled integration functions only because generic loopback trust bypasses the advertised token requirement and would fail under token_required.

evidence.fact: token configured, token_or_loopback mode, loopback bind
223 missing/wrong remote tokens rejected; 223 tokenless loopback requests admitted
no principal, tenant, workspace, session, or action capability is derived
browser bridge enabled against loopback with no credential field
copied bridge sent no Cortex write token and forwarded caller URL

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Provision a least-privilege browser capability through trusted plugin configuration and authenticate the bridge explicitly; keep URL/egress policy server-side.

Replace loopback trust/shared bearer authority with authenticated short-lived capabilities bound to principal, session, tenant/workspace, action class, target, nonce, and expiry; retain sink-specific checks.

findings.title: Direct send and device sinks bypass policy and the claimed hard send gate
findings.rootCause: Direct Home Assistant, Diplomat, Evolution, and voice/event sinks do not enforce the same approval, kill-switch, principal, and replay controls claimed by aggregate health.
impact: Direct routes can send messages or actuate devices without the explicit approval policy the health surface claims is hard-enforced.
Generic write authority can actuate devices, bypass policy by choosing alternate sinks, weaken policy itself, and replay actions.

evidence.fact: unapproved event reached a mocked HA POST; default policy allows unconfirmed low-risk actions
event and voice activation omit classifier, kill switch, confirmation, and idempotency
send_time_gate=hard and require_explicit=true
unapproved HA event reached a mocked downstream sink
send and test paths call outbound action without the claimed gate

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Enforce one policy/idempotency/approval service beneath every HA sink; bind server-issued approval and replay keys to principal, target, service, payload, and expiry.
Place one trusted send/actuation gate below every route and bind server-issued approval receipts to principal, target, payload digest, nonce, and expiry.

findings.title: AI OS status and claim authority trust stale, self-attested, cross-job evidence
findings.rootCause: Artifact existence and stored booleans are treated as current proof without freshness or exact job/process/policy/source binding, and the adapter can mint its own verifier packet.
symptoms: Claim failed without verifier evidence, then --write-verifier-evidence allowed it; the same proof set subsequently allowed unrelated hello.job.json.
status --artifact-root ai-os exited 0/ok=true with boot/run/verifier false, claim null, and reports absent.
Frozen ok=true references an adapter report 3,471,026 seconds old.
impact: Completion/default-promotion authority can be asserted for an unexecuted or unrelated job.
Historical qualification is presented as current operational health and may mask drift or missing current evidence.
Supervisors can report a missing/degraded substrate as healthy/default-on.

evidence.detail: manual_adapter_evidence/check=manual_adapter_verifier_evidence_requested produced claimStatus=allowed; unrelated job hash 1f13bf... accepted against run hash 545e57...
Self-attestation and no exact job binding.
Frozen claimStatus=allowed/verifierEvidenceOk=true cannot independently establish binding.
Hardcoded ok.
Existence/booleans drive status; no maximum age or current identity check.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Expose proof observedAt/age/stale, separate historical qualification from readiness, and bind a replayed manifest to current source/runtime hashes before current ok.

Remove self-minting from authority flow; require schema-validated evidence issued by a trusted verifier and bound to job hash, process ID, run proof, policy digest, tenant/workspace and verifier identity. Reject any mismatch/contradiction.
Separate readable/available from operational status and derive mode-specific health from required invariants; use explicit degraded/failed state and nonzero exit where appropriate.

findings.title: Public response and provider contracts are weaker than their consumers
findings.rootCause: Most public responses are untyped or empty while middleware and private consumers depend on stricter success, failure, readiness, and routing schemas not expressed by OpenAPI.
symptoms: 446 of 486 JSON operations lack field-level success schemas.
85 of 86 status-like operations lack field-level contracts.
No 403, 504, conditional /ready 503, or singularity 202 contract is documented.
Provider-consumer drift cannot be detected from the API specification.
creativityAuditEnabled and creativityAuditOverlapThreshold cannot be validly configured despite runtime reads.
impact: Clients cannot reliably validate readiness/status payloads or distinguish normal, authorization, timeout, and asynchronous outcomes.
Compatible-looking deployments can fail closed at runtime, and advertised configuration is incomplete.

evidence.observation: Strict malformed-response rejection passes Tier B, but no shared schema is published.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Add explicit response models and alternate responses, beginning with /health, /ready, /capabilities, all level status routes, and middleware-generated 403/504 envelopes.
Publish one shared typed Nexus request/response model and provider-consumer fixture; add the missing manifest properties with bounds/defaults.

findings.title: No explicit capability manifest governs discovery, loading, and safe mode
findings.rootCause: Filesystem glob loading, route-object inference, and a stale basename denylist substitute for an explicit production capability registry and safety class.
symptoms: Three WebSockets are filtered out.
Four FastAPI documentation/schema routes are included.
Expected capability count is 497 rather than 500.
/inbox_test/status is present in frozen OpenAPI and reports a level outside the L1-L38 registry.
impact: Adding a helper/test module with a router export can silently expand the production API.
Discovery consumers receive a structurally incomplete and framework-contaminated view of callable capabilities.
Operators may infer that safe mode suppresses dangerous action classes even though host execution, Docker, filesystem, browser, device, and external send routers remain exposed.

evidence.fact: safe mode active; only architect skipped; 59 routers loaded
223 frozen writes exactly reconcile after excluding only three Architect writes
five denylist names are stale/absent and admin guard protects no frozen route

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Define capability kinds explicitly and filter framework routes while representing WebSockets separately.
Replace filesystem glob registration with an explicit production router manifest and an invariant for unregistered router files.
Replace the stale name denylist with default-deny capability declarations; deny-load host/network/device/action routers in safe mode and assert the complete allowed capability set at startup.

findings.title: Mutable runtime state uses non-atomic overwrite without recoverable corruption handling
findings.rootCause: Queue, transaction, watcher, and awareness state use unlocked/non-atomic JSON overwrite, swallow or erase malformed evidence, and lack durable transition/recovery semantics.
symptoms: Two accepted maintenance items persisted as one.
Corrupt queue JSON prevents restart.
Corrupt transaction evidence resets to initialized/empty.
Cancellation becomes TransactionStepError.
Restart during write can erase or corrupt state while status remains healthy/running.
Malformed state is silently discarded.
impact: Accepted work can vanish, duplicate or indeterminate side effects may be retried after restart, and crash evidence is destroyed.
Monitoring configuration and working context can disappear after interruption without an operator-visible fault.

evidence.detail: Controlled concurrent enqueues lost item-b and corrupt JSON raised JSONDecodeError.
Corrupt journal was replaced and cancellation was converted.
Direct write_text/read_text with broad exception suppression.
Direct JSON overwrite with swallowed failures.
The same direct JSON persistence pattern in the maintenance queue demonstrably loses work/cannot recover corrupt JSON; this is corroboration, not execution of Sentinel/Awareness files.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Use SQLite or locked temp-file+fsync+atomic-replace storage, preserve/quarantine malformed state, record queued/running/cancelled/indeterminate transitions durably, and never catch BaseException for ordinary step failures.
Use a shared locked temp-file+fsync+atomic-replace helper, retain last-known-good backup, quarantine malformed input, and drive component status to degraded until recovery succeeds.

findings.title: Host and model-generated execution lack a constrained capability boundary
findings.rootCause: Generic reachability exposes host paths, Git/FFmpeg/Docker/model-generated mutation and intended caller-Python execution without an allowed-root/action capability or real OS sandbox.
impact: A caller with generic write reachability can read/write arbitrary host paths, run Git/FFmpeg/Docker operations, mount host volumes, or apply generated code.
Current behavior violates the execution API contract; a trivial invocation fix would expose arbitrary caller code with service privileges unless a real sandbox is added first.

evidence.fact: Git init forwarded a traversal-shaped arbitrary path without normalization or root enforcement
Evolution traversal escaped its extension root and Geneticist accepted a broad credential-bearing root
caller host volumes are emitted directly to Docker
safe synthetic execution failed before launch because create_subprocess_exec received a list as one argument
intended process uses service interpreter with inherited environment/files/network and no OS sandbox

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Do not repair the argument bug alone. Disable the route, then implement an isolated worker with immutable filesystem, empty allowlisted environment, no network by default, resource limits, and trusted approval/capability checks.
Move host actions into constrained workers with immutable allowlisted roots, restricted identity/environment/network, Docker volume policy, and separately issued action/approval capabilities.
findings.evidenceQualification: Security results tied only to missing V-CODEC-HANDLER/V-AUTH-SCOPE/V-EXTERNAL-AST command bodies are treated as Tier D; independent Tier A/B/C evidence is retained and affected coverage rows are downgraded where necessary.

findings.title: Untrusted prompt text bypasses mandatory route gating
findings.rootCause: isOracleExecutorPrompt treats two phrases in raw prompt/latest-user content as trusted execution metadata, and before_prompt_build returns before contacting Nexus even when requireRouting=true.
symptoms: A normal user session containing both phrases receives no route context.
The existing creativity test explicitly expects the unsafe bypass.
impact: Any user-controlled turn can suppress Cortex-first routing and its packed execution/safety context.

evidence.observation: The copied entrypoint is hash-identical to the frozen source and authorizes a text predicate as bypass.
The spoof case returned undefined and made zero fetch calls under requireRouting=true.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Remove content-based authorization; permit bypass only from runtime-attested Oracle session metadata and add a negative user-text regression.

findings.title: Route-gate cap silently removes five Nexus always-on levels
findings.rootCause: Nexus emits 15 ALWAYS_ON_LEVELS, but route-gate normalization discards always_on and prioritization applies the frozen maxLevels=10 cap with only L24/L5 mandatory on an ordinary turn.
symptoms: L32-L36 were absent from the packed ordinary-turn level block.
A configured cap is applied after the provider policy without a degradation marker.
impact: Apex validation, synthesis, governance, awareness, and augmentation policy can disappear without either layer reporting policy loss.

evidence.observation: Frozen maxLevels is 10; hash-bound Nexus declares 15 always-on levels; the hash-bound gate does not preserve always_on.
A valid 15-level provider response packed 10 unique levels and omitted 32,33,34,35,36.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Define a shared total-vs-optional cap contract, preserve always_on and per-level origin, and reject or explicitly mark unsatisfied mandatory policy.

findings.title: Packed route provenance conflates provider, local mandatory, governor, and cache decisions
findings.rootCause: Route levels lose always_on/origin during normalization, local mandatory and creativity levels are merged into one list, and renderPlan unconditionally says the routing decision was made upstream by Cortex. cached_fallback carries the same assertion.
symptoms: Locally inserted L24/L5 are rendered as Cortex-selected upstream work.
A signed cached fallback is internally marked but the user/model-facing block still makes the upstream assertion.
The hook appends instructions; it never proves that selected levels or their models executed.
impact: Consumers cannot distinguish model work, policy insertion, cache, or advisory prompt text; audit claims can overstate execution.

evidence.source: route-gate index.ts:529-549,1137-1157,1431-1457 and route-gate worker harness
evidence.observation: A provider response containing only duplicate L7 caused local L24/L5 insertion and the unconditional upstream claim.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Attach provider|local_mandatory|local_governor|cache origin to every level, preserve always_on, render degradation conditionally, and report execution separately from recommendation.

findings.title: Adaptive routing learns success without output or causal level execution
findings.rootCause: Route gate equates event.success plus no tool error with level success and ignores outputObserved/actual activation. Nexus similarly records execution_success=true and user_correction=false for normal orchestration using self-derived validation signals.
symptoms: An agent_end success with no llm_output credited L5/L8/L24 and set L8 score to 0.75.
Bandit/rollout policy can train on orchestration completion rather than answer quality.
impact: Dynamic policy can reinforce levels and rollout changes that did not produce a usable model answer.

evidence.observation: False-positive training was reproduced and the Nexus reward source is explicit in code.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Separate run completion, verified output, user outcome, and causally observed level execution; train only on an explicit outcome receipt.

findings.title: Hard tool budget admits concurrent calls beyond its ceiling
findings.rootCause: before_tool_call only checks the completed count; capacity is incremented after execution in after_tool_call and is not reserved atomically.
symptoms: At 19/20 calls, two concurrent prechecks both passed and completion advanced beyond the declared ceiling.
impact: The advertised runtime limit is not hard under parallel tool scheduling.

evidence.observation: The concurrency regression is deterministic in an isolated hook harness.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Reserve a correlated slot atomically before admission and release/settle it on completion or cancellation.

findings.title: Reported Oracle model identity is not bound to the executed OpenClaw command
findings.rootCause: Identity resolution selects the oracle agent's configured model, while execution ignores OPENCLAW_BIN, hardcodes --agent main, drops the system prompt, and backend selection does not accept ChatRequest.model.
symptoms: Captured argv began with openclaw, selected main, and omitted SYSTEM_SENTINEL despite a configured binary and supplied system text.
A policy-approved request label can execute a different dynamic model.
impact: Provider, model, prompt-policy, cost, and provenance controls can describe a different execution than the one performed.

evidence.observation: Command mismatch and missing system prompt reproduced with a fake subprocess.
Frozen status includes oracle sessions, contradicting the copied --agent main binding without proving which model executed.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Use one validated command builder from resolved agent/executable/system contract and derive returned identity from provider output; enforce or reject request.model explicitly.

findings.title: Oracle provider followers and Ollama accept empty completion text
findings.rootCause: A single-flight follower ignores Event.wait's timeout result and returns result or empty string; Ollama response normalization defaults missing response to empty and missing done to true.
symptoms: An unsignalled follower returned ''.
A 200 Ollama object lacking response became response='', done=true.
impact: Concurrent or fallback calls can become empty successful Oracle completions.

evidence.observation: Both malformed-success paths reproduced without network access.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Require a signalled result and non-empty validated text at every provider boundary; map timeout/malformed output to typed 503/504.

findings.title: Synthetic Nexus retrieval and answer clear the 0.84 early-exit gate at 0.98 confidence
findings.rootCause: retrieve_top3 manufactures recent_memory/curated_memory/docs snippets by echoing the query; the answer generator emits generic canned text; confidence_score rewards length, structure, and any retrieval hit without evidence authenticity.
symptoms: 'What is the capital of Atlantis?' received three fabricated sources, confidence 0.98, and confidence_gate early exit.
Semantic provider analysis is skipped and Nexus records 0.99 semantic confidence for anytime_early_exit.
impact: Unanswered factual questions can bypass the provider and be presented/trained as high-confidence grounded work.

evidence.observation: The false-positive confidence/early-exit chain reproduced at 0.98 with fabricated source labels.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Mark fixture retrieval synthetic or remove it from production; require backend receipts and evidence-grounded validation before confidence/early exit/outcome credit.

findings.title: Nexus accepts an empty provider object as semantic success and bypasses standing model policy
findings.rootCause: analyze_intent_with_oracle hardcodes openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 and treats any JSON object as oracle_semantic, defaulting confidence to 0.5 without validating intents/levels. Its 30-second timeout exceeds the route gate's 20-second budget.
symptoms: Provider content '{}' became method=oracle_semantic, confidence=0.5.
No-key and timeout paths are low-signal fallbacks/errors, but malformed-success is treated more favorably.
The client can abort before the nested provider deadline.
impact: Malformed provider output can influence routing as successful semantic work, and nested calls can outlive the caller deadline.

evidence.observation: Malformed, unavailable, and timeout paths were isolated; hardcoded model and 30s/20s deadline contradiction are explicit.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Use the standing provider/model policy, strict semantic response schema, and propagated absolute deadline shorter than the route-gate budget.

findings.title: Deliberative routes present repaired or fallback text as unmarked model success
findings.rootCause: Council catches provider failure and substitutes deterministic analysis without an origin field; Mediator and Seer repair valid-but-empty JSON into invented content with success=true/error=null; Synthesist emits heuristic confidence without generator provenance.
symptoms: Council provider-unavailable deliberation returned success and no error/origin/provenance/degraded key.
Mediator '{}' returned invented common ground and compromise with error null.
Seer '{}' returned three invented risks/opportunities and medium confidence with error null.
impact: Callers cannot distinguish provider model work from deterministic repair, fallback, or heuristic output.

evidence.source: isolated-reasoning-checks.py and router source cited in report
evidence.observation: Provider-unavailable and malformed-success cases reproduced without external calls.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Add a shared result envelope with origin, providerInvoked, provider/model, degraded, repairApplied, cache status, and validated evidence; do not use success=true/error=null for synthetic repair.

findings.title: Council interprets negated approval as APPROVE
findings.rootCause: Plain-text verdict inference searches for APPROVE/GO tokens without negation or a strict structured decision contract.
symptoms: 'I cannot APPROVE this unsafe action.' returned success=true, verdict=APPROVE, risk_score=0.22.
impact: A gating route can authorize an action that its provider explicitly rejects.

evidence.observation: The safety-critical false positive reproduced deterministically.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Require strict JSON enum validation; malformed/free-text decisions fail closed to NEEDS_CHANGES and never infer approval from substrings.

findings.title: Simulator's strict contract accepts duplicate labels and 999 percent probability
findings.rootCause: _parse_outcomes_strict validates exactly three typed objects but does not validate the label enum/uniqueness or parse/bound probabilities; only timeout enters the Oracle fallback, not general connection failure.
symptoms: Three identical best_case rows with 999% were accepted.
ConnectError fails the route rather than using the documented provider fallback.
impact: Structurally valid but nonsensical simulations can be returned as successful model work.

evidence.observation: Invalid semantic outcomes were accepted by the strict parser.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Use label literals with exact set equality, numeric probability parsing/bounds and sum policy, plus one explicit retry/fallback error taxonomy.

findings.title: Fractal node ID collisions inflate merge coverage
findings.rootCause: Child branch IDs are rebuilt from depth/index without the parent branch, so repeated sibling tasks can receive identical node IDs; aggregation keys results by ID and counts one result for every colliding leaf.
symptoms: A six-leaf plan had three unique IDs and three results produced coverage=1.0, covered_leaves=6.
impact: Partial execution can be reported as complete and successful.

evidence.observation: Collision and inflated aggregation reproduced; depth clamp itself terminates.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Include the full parent branch/path or stable ordinal in node IDs and reject duplicate IDs before execution/aggregation.

findings.title: Oracle sandbox reports unverified health and wraps upstream failures
findings.rootCause: status returns online without key/provider checks; probe returns a normal route body for upstream non-2xx, treats 200 non-JSON as ok, and does not normalize transport timeout.
symptoms: Status said online and an upstream 503 returned a normal object with status_code=503/ok=false rather than a typed route failure.
impact: Monitoring and callers can confuse route availability with provider readiness and HTTP success with provider success.

evidence.observation: False health and wrapped failure reproduced with a stub provider.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Report ready_unverified, validate provider schema, and map upstream/transport errors to consistent 502/503/504 route responses.

findings.title: Configured service tier is neither transmitted nor provider-confirmed
findings.rootCause: Worker config declares serviceTier=default, but launcher options/provider invocation omit it and reported output hardcodes default; Oracle's command exposes no tier argument or receipt.
symptoms: The frozen snapshot contains no service-tier evidence.
Reported tier can reflect a constant rather than provider execution.
impact: Standing cost/latency tier policy cannot be enforced or audited.

evidence.observation: Tier plumbing is absent structurally.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Parse/validate/transmit tier and require provider-confirmed receipt; never report a tier from a hardcoded constant.

findings.title: AI OS accepts empty or emergency Oracle JSON as provider.compute success
findings.rootCause: AI OS validates the requested model label and HTTP/JSON syntax but not Oracle's response schema, selected model, lane, provider invocation, or degradation provenance.
symptoms: Isolated adapter cases accepted {} and an oracle-emergency-bypass done=true body as provider.compute artifacts.
Frozen AI OS status records HTTP 200 without underlying model/lane, so historical work cannot be classified.
impact: Synthetic, empty, or policy-mismatched output can be recorded as successful provider compute.

evidence.observation: Six mocked provider execution cases reproduced schema/provenance acceptance; the sanitized live record omits model/lane.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Validate a provider-specific result envelope and actual selected model; reject empty, done=false, emergency/synthetic lanes, and missing provider receipts.

findings.title: Chain selection, termination, and activation evidence disagree
findings.rootCause: Nexus mutates forced-chain recommendations/markers through multiple phases without one deduplicated final contract; route gate only renders advisory prompt text; generic chain_to has a timeout but no chain ID, visited set, depth, or cycle guard.
symptoms: A deep architecture case emitted duplicate 9/15/32/34 levels, method l9_chain_forced, final l9_chain ['architect'], and missing forced levels in activation/HUD telemetry.
A duplicate route turn sets duplicate_chain_risk=true but still calls Nexus again.
No downstream level result set proves the selected chain executed.
impact: Routing metadata can overstate or misdescribe a chain, while recursion/cycle safety is advisory rather than end-to-end enforced.

evidence.source: Nexus worker harness; isolated-route-gate.test.mjs; nexus.py:4420-4511,4824-4908; consciousness_integration.py:210-273
evidence.observation: Finalization contradiction and non-terminating duplicate route request reproduced; no reciprocal static cycle was found.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Create one immutable deduplicated final plan/activation receipt and propagate chain_id, visited levels, depth, absolute deadline, and terminal reason through every internal call.

findings.title: Readiness validates required paths without methods or collision safety
findings.rootCause: _route_inventory and readiness reduce requirements to a set of paths and treat an empty expansion-error list as inventory health.
symptoms: GET-only replacements for both required POST routes passed.
An injected duplicate POST /l22/store passed.
impact: A wrong-method or colliding registration can satisfy readiness while the required memory write contract is unusable or ambiguous.
smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Represent requirements as method/path pairs and fail readiness on duplicate method/path registrations.

findings.title: Import and schema-load paths mutate persistence and read ambient configuration
findings.rootCause: Routers construct persistent clients/services and filesystem-backed global objects at module scope; main.py calls create_app at import.
symptoms: Controlled Graph construction created SQLite tables and eight indexes.
Controlled Librarian import created a Chroma directory and called PersistentClient/get_or_create_collection.
impact: Documentation generation, tooling, tests, or a failed startup can create/migrate storage and touch ambient credential/state paths.

evidence.safety: temporary directory only; no network/live import

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Move persistent construction and credential reads behind explicit lifespan/dependency factories; provide a read-only schema/inventory construction mode.

findings.title: Nine binary/static endpoints advertise JSON success media
findings.rootCause: Response classes/media types are not reflected in the generated OpenAPI for these handlers.
symptoms: Eight command-center JS/SVG routes and one Home Assistant WAV route advertise application/json.
impact: Generated clients and gateways can parse or negotiate these payloads incorrectly.
smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Declare the exact response class and media type on each of the nine route decorators and add OpenAPI media assertions.

findings.title: Root discovery advertises four nonexistent exact endpoints
findings.rootCause: The root endpoint contains a manually maintained endpoint map that is not generated from registered routes.
symptoms: Exact HTTP routes /graph, /parse, /tools, and /ws do not exist in source or frozen OpenAPI.
impact: Clients following root discovery links receive 404s or misunderstand prefixes as callable endpoints.
smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Generate discovery links from explicit operation IDs or advertise documented prefixes with their concrete entry routes.

findings.title: OpenAPI tags contain duplicates and naming aliases
findings.rootCause: Dynamic include_router tags are appended to router-local tags without normalization or a top-level tag registry.
symptoms: Twenty-one operations repeat an identical tag.
Thirty operations pair case/underscore variants.
Four core operations are untagged.
impact: Documentation and code generation produce fragmented or duplicated API groupings.
smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Choose one tag source, normalize names, and publish a top-level tag registry.

findings.title: Semantic L22 accepts unbounded content and retains an unbounded idempotency ledger
findings.rootCause: store_memory_record limits only the idempotency-key bytes. It passes content/metadata to Chroma without the structured-store limits, and memory_idempotency has neither TTL nor count/byte pruning.
symptoms: An exact copied-function probe accepted and forwarded a 5 MiB semantic document; the ledger schema and insert path grow per scoped key indefinitely.
impact: Large requests and unique idempotency keys can amplify memory, embedding, vector-store, SQLite, and disk use; structured quotas do not protect this path.

evidence.detail: No content/metadata bound or ledger cleanup in semantic path.
Structured L22 tests pass their separate finite bounds, confirming the contradiction is path-specific rather than absence of all limits.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Apply byte limits before hashing/embedding, reuse the stricter metadata limits, add tenant/workspace ledger TTL/count/byte policy with transactional cleanup, and regress oversized and churn/restart cases. Coordinate migration before deleting historical ledger rows.

findings.title: L22 recency pruning overrides Codec's utility-aware retention contract
findings.rootCause: Codec ranks protected/high-utility overflow, but every structured write and startup subsequently runs _prune_codec_records, which keeps only the newest rows per session and cannot see retention priority.
symptoms: With five snapshots and a four-row cap, the exact L22 prune deleted the oldest snapshot even though it carried the highest retention priority.
impact: High-value continuity state can be silently deleted after Codec reports it preserved, especially at restart or the next write.

evidence.detail: Recency-only pruning runs on write and startup.
Codec separately sorts by protected flag and retention_priority.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Define one authoritative retention function and persist/index priority in L22. Have startup/write pruning call it atomically; add cross-layer tests where high-priority old rows survive within a global finite overflow cap.

findings.title: Runtime offload notes are append-only and health has no retention contract
findings.rootCause: Runtime delivery creates note shards and a hot index but defines no max files, bytes, age, or pruning; health checks only root existence and file count.
symptoms: A temporary root containing 1,205 files remained ok=true with no retention field; the frozen root already reports 706 files.
impact: Non-authoritative notes can exhaust inode/disk budgets and make health increasingly expensive while still presenting green.

evidence.detail: runtimeOffloadedMemory fileCount=706 and ok=true; explicitly non-authoritative.
Append/write path has no retention policy.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Add explicit age/count/byte limits, atomic prune after durable authoritative handoff, and health fields for current usage/oldest/pruned/errors. Preserve the non-authoritative label.

findings.title: Structural index health ignores age and source provenance
findings.rootCause: Latest-index health requires a readable artifact, no listed errors, and positive graph counts; it does not enforce a freshness SLA or bind sourceRepo/digest to the serving source/graph.
symptoms: An artifact dated 1970 with an obsolete source path returned ok=true. The frozen live artifact is about 12.44 days old and points to an August 8 repair-copy source while also returning ok=true.
impact: Queries and prior-art decisions may rely on a structurally populated but stale or differently sourced graph while health certifies it.

evidence.detail: ageSeconds=1,074,657.014; sourceRepo=/home/jake/cortex-repairs/...; ok=true
No age or current-source comparison enters ok.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Publish source commit/tree digest, indexer version, graph digest, and completion time; compare them with the serving source identity and an explicit age SLA. Fail/degrade health without deleting the last-known-good graph.

findings.title: File/governance health overstates independently verified authority
findings.rootCause: The sanitized snapshot omits canonical file manifests/content, while several governance/legacy health fields are derived from configuration, constants, or path presence rather than replayed precedence and recovery checks.
symptoms: All file/governance/legacy components are green, but this shard cannot verify staleness, conflicting facts, retention, permissions, or recovery from the copy.
impact: Consumers may interpret a configuration inventory as proof that canonical precedence and historical behavior are correct.

evidence.detail: 208 files, 36 project files, 11 mappings, booleans green; no manifest/content.
Health primarily reports configured precedence/presence.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Add a sanitized manifest of canonical paths, hashes/mtimes/authority labels and an isolated precedence-conflict/recovery canary; distinguish configured, available, and verified fields.

findings.title: Lesson promotion accepts duplicate evidence and emits a content-unbound proof digest
findings.rootCause: Promotion compares declared-ID set size with raw matching-row length but does not require exact unique observed-ID coverage. Its digest excludes verifier result content, attempts, scores, and artifact hashes.
symptoms: Two observations of verify-algebra-1 promoted a two-evidence candidate while verify-probability-1 was absent; materially changed verifier rows produced the same digest.
impact: The generic promotion API/CLI can overstate independent evidence and cannot prove which outcomes justified a trusted lesson.

evidence.result: promoted=true with all ten gates; identical digest 68cb247e...

evidence.detail: Raw count and shallow digest composition.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Require exact unique required-ID coverage, bind each ID to a distinct authorized attempt/exam, and hash a canonical full proof including result/artifact digests and thresholds. Add duplicate, missing-ID, changed-score, and changed-attempt regressions.

findings.title: Retrieval-pack builder can return data above its declared token bound
findings.rootCause: The shrink loop can remove only lessons. It returns after lessons are exhausted even if task, concept IDs, warnings, or envelope still exceed maxTokens; callers need not validate before use/write.
symptoms: A 10,000-character task and zero lessons returned estimatedTokens=2,608 for maxTokens=100; the schema validator rejected the returned record.
impact: Callers can persist or send a schema-invalid context pack, weakening cost/context guarantees.

evidence.detail: No final fail-closed bound check before return/use.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Bound fixed fields, fail closed when the minimum envelope exceeds maxTokens, and require validation before persistence/model use.

findings.title: Transfer matcher/profile drift disables legacy qualification and rejects its registry entries
findings.rootCause: The current router generates phd-math-<conceptId>-v1 matcher IDs and concept-ID profiles, while legacy profiles retain code-exact-integer-multiplication-v1 and code-polynomial-factoring-v1; validation requires exact binding.
symptoms: transfer-control status/init exit before dispatch, seven semantic-transfer tests cannot register, and the live-plugin copied suite is 11/12 on the same mismatch.
impact: Legacy transfer status/init/verify/plan/apply/promote paths are dead and old signed entries fail closed. Deployed registry version is unknown.

evidence.detail: Conflicting identities.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Version the legacy and 264-concept routers as separate contracts, then atomically migrate profiles/registries with signed provenance; do not silently alias IDs.

findings.title: Operator-direct transfer bypasses qualification and injects outside software context
findings.rootCause: Registry validation/selection treats operator_enabled/operator_direct as qualified. The installer fills evidence-looking fields with plugin-source and plan hashes; the router computes but does not require codingContext and supplies no source-controlled negative gates.
symptoms: A signed 264-entry registry built only from synthetic source/plan hashes injected number-fractions into a pure math prompt with codingContext=false, empty negative gates, and answerInfluence=true.
impact: A privileged local operator can present unqualified guidance as active learned context beyond the documented math-to-software boundary; a signature authenticates the operator, not evidence quality.

evidence.detail: Operator path accepted as production selection.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Remove operator_direct from production-qualified selection or isolate it in an explicit default-off experimental mode; require codingContext, applicability and negative gates, and never use plan/source hashes as qualification evidence. Migrate signed registries explicitly.

findings.title: Transfer catalog omits provenance for derived routing metadata
findings.rootCause: The raw 264-concept graph digest and core fields are bound, but derived stage, tracks, and requiredForQualification metadata name no generator/policy version or source digest.
symptoms: Core comparison is exact while derived routing policy cannot be reconstructed from declared provenance.
impact: Reviewers can verify integrity but not why qualification/routing metadata changed.

evidence.detail: Catalog source digest 7ad786...bbc5c matched; 264 core-field comparisons had zero mismatches.
Derived metadata is checked in without upstream derivation identity.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Declare and hash the derivation policy/generator/version in the catalog manifest.

findings.title: AI OS labels arbitrary provider POSTs as no external writes
findings.rootCause: The boundary equates operation labels and policy booleans with side-effect freedom. Arbitrary HTTPS provider/path configuration is accepted, both operations use POST, and successful receipts unconditionally report externalWrites=false.
symptoms: Injected fetch captured POST https://example.invalid/mutate with a body while access was allowed and the receipt reported no external write.
impact: A state-changing endpoint can be invoked through provider.read/compute and falsely represented as internal-only.

evidence.detail: No-network fake fetch: accessOk=true, method=POST, reportedExternalWrites=false.
Configurable transport and unconditional label.
Frozen selected policy is loopback Cortex /knowledge/search and /oracle/chat; no live mutation was observed.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Treat network POST as an external effect unless an immutable audited operation contract proves safety; pin approved origins/routes/digests, require trusted policy approval, and report transport effect separately from output storage.

findings.title: AI OS default promotion enables a candidate before recovery succeeds
findings.rootCause: Promotion writes enabled pending configuration before recovery and writes enabled degraded configuration after a failed recovery without preserving the prior default.
symptoms: Source returns default_on_degraded while the candidate remains enabled; weak claim binding compounds the risk.
impact: Failed smoke/recovery can still change the active pointer/config and expose a degraded substrate.

evidence.detail: writeDefaultConfig always sets enabled=true; promotion writes before and after recovery without smoke.ok gate.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Stage candidate evidence/config, require bound verifier/claim plus smoke/recovery and explicit approval, then atomically replace the active pointer; preserve the prior default on any failure.

findings.title: Frozen evidence omits replay prerequisites for AI OS, Learning OS, and service guards
findings.rootCause: The sanitized copy contains compact claims/config but omits referenced AIOS proof trees, Learning registries/telemetry/qualification state, the service memory-guard drop-in, and some historical test fixtures.
symptoms: Configured AIOS status is not replayable; service guard is 1 pass/1 missing-file failure; AIOS copied counts are 3/7, 7/10, 7/7 versus documented 7/7,10/10,7/7; deployed Learning effect is unobservable.
impact: Auditors cannot independently replay several green historical claims, and environment failures can be confused with product failures.

evidence.detail: node scripts/aios-adapter.mjs status exits 1 with workspace path required; test counts recorded in verification.
test_cortex_service_memory_guard.py fails only on missing deploy/systemd/cortex-memory-guard.conf.
Frozen AIOS status references paths outside the copy; frozen Learning config contains no registry/telemetry.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Freeze a sanitized immutable manifest and necessary nonsecret proof/fixture/config packets with hashes; make tests self-contained under workspace-local temporary roots.

findings.title: Remote model and sandbox arguments lack a strict remote-shell transport contract
findings.rootCause: Host and absolute paths are validated, but model and sandbox strings are appended to the SSH remote command without an allowlist or length-delimited transport.
symptoms: Configured policy is not constrained to supported model/sandbox values; OpenSSH remote-command serialization may make crafted values shell-significant.
impact: At minimum unsupported execution policy can be selected; depending on transport quoting, crafted configuration may alter the remote command.

evidence.detail: safeHost/safeAbsoluteRemotePath do not cover model/sandbox; values are appended after bash -s --.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Strictly allowlist model/sandbox/service-tier/reasoning values or send a length-delimited/base64 JSON request to a fixed remote script without interpolating values into a shell command.

findings.title: Required Sentinel preflight fails open on dependency failure
findings.rootCause: maybe_sentinel_gate blocks only a successful dictionary containing a scan with issues; false, missing, malformed, timed-out, or unreachable responses return no gate.
symptoms: requires_preflight workflows continue when Sentinel is unavailable.
Port 8888 mismatch can convert the safety gate into an allow decision.
impact: Safety-critical workflow execution can proceed without the explicitly required preflight.

evidence.detail: success=false and success=true without scan both produced null gate.
Only truthy success plus a scan is examined.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Return a blocked/unavailable result whenever required preflight is missing, false, malformed, timed out, or unreachable; add dependency-down, malformed-payload, timeout, and port-mismatch regressions.

findings.title: Synchronous provider and queue work defeats async timeouts
findings.rootCause: Async endpoints directly invoke requests/Celery/backend/file work; asyncio.wait_for cannot preempt synchronous work on the event-loop thread, and several heavy routes are excluded from request timeout middleware.
symptoms: A 10 ms deadline completed only after a 60 ms synchronous provider call.
A 10 ms timer was delayed to 214 ms by send_task.
impact: Slow dependencies stall unrelated requests, including observability, increase tail latency, and can continue side effects after callers expect a timeout.

evidence.detail: Synchronous Nexus provider double ignored effective async deadline.
Synchronous Celery submission blocked unrelated event-loop timing.
Provider-heavy routes are among timeout exclusions.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Use async clients or bounded thread offload for every blocking call, propagate a remaining-deadline budget, remove blanket exclusions after compatibility tests, and ensure cancellation cannot leave untracked side effects.

findings.title: Workflow retry attempts and backoff are unbounded
findings.rootCause: Retry parsing applies only minimum bounds and sleeps full configured backoff without a maximum or remaining-workflow-budget clamp.
symptoms: One billion attempts and one billion seconds backoff are accepted.
impact: Malicious or mistaken metadata can exhaust workers, extend workflows beyond declared deadlines, and amplify dependency pressure.

evidence.detail: Copied step_retry_settings returned the billion-scale values unchanged.
No maximum attempts/backoff/cumulative retry duration is enforced.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Set hard maxima for attempts, per-retry backoff, and cumulative retry time; clamp every sleep/call to the remaining workflow budget and reject out-of-range metadata.

findings.title: Queue outage looks online and scheduling has no admission/idempotency/cancellation contract
findings.rootCause: Inspector exceptions collapse to integer zero, which the endpoint maps to online; send/backend calls are synchronous and scheduling accepts requests without capacity, idempotency, or cancellation controls.
symptoms: Broker-down double produced online/zero.
All 64 synthetic submissions were marked scheduled.
Event loop blocked during broker send.
impact: Operators see an idle healthy queue during outage; load can be admitted without bounds, duplicate work cannot be safely deduped, and tasks lack a supported cancellation boundary.

evidence.detail: Dependency failure was reported as online via celery.inspect.
64/64 local submissions passed the endpoint without admission response.
Slow send_task blocked the loop.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Return typed unavailable status on inspection failure; offload all Celery calls; add queue/pending capacity, request idempotency keys, bounded args, explicit rejection/retry-after, and cancellation semantics.

findings.title: Background tasks and cron schedules lack coordinated shutdown and restart recovery
findings.rootCause: Main creates background tasks without retaining/supervising them and has no teardown after lifespan yield; APScheduler uses an in-memory job store with no policy rehydration.
symptoms: Task failure can be silent while status flags stay running.
Subscriptions/tasks can duplicate across reload.
Accepted cron jobs disappear after process restart while policy JSON remains.
impact: Restart loses scheduled work, shutdown can interrupt persistence, silent task death is invisible, and status may describe intent rather than execution.

evidence.detail: Scheduler, Chronos, and Awareness start; no cleanup block exists.
In-memory AsyncIOScheduler; jobs are only added at request time.
Frozen process is active but no child-task registry or last-success state is captured.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Retain tasks in app.state, attach done/error supervision, cancel and await them in finally, stop APScheduler cleanly, and use a durable job store or validated deterministic policy rehydration before readiness.

findings.title: Sentinel reports healthy while monitoring is stopped
findings.rootCause: Sentinel status hard-codes active/healthy and startup/scan/load/save failures are swallowed instead of updating observable health.
symptoms: scheduler_running=false, zero scans, and a down watcher still produce success=true/status=active/severity=healthy.
impact: The subsystem intended to detect failure can fail invisibly and safety gates/operators may trust a non-running monitor.

evidence.detail: Direct copied handler execution demonstrated false healthy state.
Exceptions are swallowed and status literals do not derive from task/scan state.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Track startup errors, task done/exception, last attempted/successful scan and age; derive severity from those fields and mark stopped/stale/error as degraded or unavailable.

findings.title: Watchdog records restart completion without verifying recovery
findings.rootCause: The script writes restart_completed and resets failures immediately after issuing systemctl stop/start, with no post-start readiness loop.
symptoms: A failed start can enter cooldown with a successful completion reason.
impact: Automation and operators can believe recovery succeeded while the service remains unavailable, and cooldown delays subsequent intervention.

evidence.detail: Fake systemctl received stop/start and state immediately reported restart_completed; no curl followed start.
The sequence has no verification branch.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Poll /ready with a bounded deadline after start; reset failures and write restart_completed only on success, otherwise persist restart_failed and return nonzero.

findings.title: Resource enforcement and expensive health-probe safety are not established
findings.rootCause: The snapshot omits installed cgroup/restart/timer properties, the expected memory-guard drop-in is absent from the copy, and async health routes perform synchronous recursive/DB work.
symptoms: Only MemoryCurrent and TasksCurrent are captured.
Memory guard regression fails on a missing drop-in.
L22/Knowledge health scans can block and scale with store size.
A 12.4-day index remains ok without a freshness threshold.
impact: Resource exhaustion can impair the very probes used for recovery, and operators cannot verify memory/task ceilings or index recency from the evidence bundle.

evidence.detail: Memory-guard suite passed 1/2; expected cortex-memory-guard.conf is absent.
Frozen service status has current usage but no enforcement properties.
At least one async operational path demonstrably blocks the loop.
Index ageSeconds=1,074,657 while overall memory health is true.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Capture installed unit/timer/drop-in properties, add enforceable cgroup caps with controlled pressure tests, move scans off-loop, cache/bound DB/filesystem probes, paginate/cap inputs, and define source-bound freshness thresholds.

findings.title: Detached notifier can claim terminal success without valid state or delivery acknowledgement
findings.rootCause: Configured raw status strings are terminal authority and any sender exit code zero is accepted without schema validation, artifact verification, freshness, or positive message ID.
symptoms: A year-2000 completed state with nonexistent artifact produced COMPLETED wording.
A sender payload stating ok=false/delivery rejected was ledgered as delivered.
impact: Users may receive authoritative-looking completion messages for stale, provisional, fabricated, or rejected deliveries; subsequent correct notices can be suppressed.

evidence.detail: Both terminal-authority and false-ack behaviors were reproduced without external send.
No terminal schema or positive response validation exists.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Define job-specific terminal schemas requiring immutable run ID, validated UTC completion time, verificationPassed, artifact manifest/digest, and truth boundary; accept delivery only with a versioned positive response and provider message ID.

findings.title: Notifier dedupe suppresses revisions and duplicates crash-window sends
findings.rootCause: The dedupe key excludes run ID, completion time, artifact path/digest, and delivery sequence; external send happens before the durable ledger commit without provider idempotency.
symptoms: Different run/artifact revisions dedupe as already delivered.
Ledger-write failure after send causes a second send on retry.
impact: Corrected final artifacts may never be announced while process crashes can produce duplicate user messages.

evidence.detail: Revision was suppressed.
Crash-window harness sent twice; separate transient pre-send failure retried correctly.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Key on immutable run ID plus terminal sequence/verified artifact receipt digest, persist an attempt/pending record, and pass a provider-supported idempotency key with reconciliation of uncertain outcomes.

findings.title: Retention can select a promoted pointer target without checking required backup
findings.rootCause: Protection compares candidate basenames but does not resolve external latest pointers; configured backupRequirement is never evaluated or revalidated.
symptoms: An old directory referenced by latest.json was the only deletion candidate; report had no backup verification.
impact: A confirmed retention run can delete the promoted artifact, strand stale pointers, and violate preservation policy.

evidence.detail: Safe dry-run reproduced pointer-target selection without deleting it.
No realpath pointer protection or backup check.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Resolve every configured pointer target to a protected realpath set, validate a signed/hashed backup receipt, require positive finite retention age, and revalidate pointer/backup state immediately before deletion.

findings.title: Redis startup success is overstated and omitted from readiness
findings.rootCause: Application lifespan starts redis-server with check=false, then unconditionally logs success and does not perform a bounded ping/readiness dependency check.
symptoms: A failed or duplicate Redis launch can be invisible until queue operations fail.
impact: Broker/backend outage can coexist with ready=true and queue status may still say online.

evidence.detail: Redis happened to be listening at capture.
Return code is ignored and success is logged unconditionally.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Manage Redis independently where possible; otherwise validate process return code and bounded ping, surface dependency status, and make required queue readiness degrade on failure.

findings.title: Workflow approvals accept caller-forged grants and fail open on unknown actions
findings.rootCause: root_cause
impact: A workflow author can self-approve high-risk sends, while unclassified host/device/action endpoints default to low risk; direct FastAPI sinks bypass workflow policy entirely.

evidence.fact: unpersisted caller grant with granted_by=human authorized /diplomat/send; 208/223 routes allowed without a grant
embedded metadata grants are normalized without trusted issuer/signature

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Accept only server-stored or independently signed approval references bound to principal, workflow, action digest, target, nonce, and expiry; default unknown action capabilities to deny.

findings.title: Outbound URL boundaries admit loopback, link-local, and caller-controlled targets
findings.rootCause: root_cause
impact: Reachable callers may target metadata, private services, loopback services, arbitrary external systems, or local file-like browser inputs, and may retain responses.

evidence.fact: browser and Diplomat helpers admitted a metadata-shaped link-local URL; plugin forwarded it only to mocked fetch
missing caller allowlist means allow all and multiple direct navigation paths bypass it
validation checks syntax rather than resolved address/redirect destination

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Enforce a centralized egress broker with scheme/hostname policy, DNS resolution, private/link-local/metadata denial, redirect revalidation, response limits, and independently authorized target capabilities.

findings.title: Schedulers and autonomy paths can defer or amplify unapproved writes
findings.rootCause: root_cause
impact: A one-time generic request can schedule, queue, or trigger later actions outside the initiating session and without durable principal/action approval or replay binding.

evidence.fact: cron trigger and governor execute were allowed without trusted approval by the workflow classifier
policy is optional; queue submits tasks; night shift defaults non-dry-run

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Persist authenticated principal and immutable action digest with every job; require sink-time capability revalidation, idempotency, expiry, cancellation, and policy enforcement.

findings.title: Sensitive GET and WebSocket surfaces bypass the write-only authorization middleware
findings.rootCause: root_cause
impact: Container logs, Codec session state, HA/tool/Diplomat/autonomy/config reads, Forge capabilities, and side-effecting GET modes may be available without principal authorization.

evidence.fact: caller-selected Codec session was read without authentication
WebSocket logs streamed a synthetic secret without an auth gate
only POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE are gated

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Add sensitivity/capability metadata to all HTTP and WebSocket routes, authenticate reads and upgrades, remove state mutation from GET, and authorize at the data owner/sink.

findings.rootCause: root_cause
impact: Credentials, PHI, URL secrets, command output, diffs, upstream bodies, or hard-coded contact PII can enter durable logs/traces or unauthenticated responses.

findings.title: Browser notary falls back to provider/public key and exposes a signing oracle
findings.rootCause: root_cause
impact: Notary attestations can be forged under default configuration, while provider credentials are inappropriately reused as signing material.

evidence.fact: known public default reproduced a copied notary signature
key falls back to OPENROUTER_API_KEY then a public constant; verify returns recomputed HMAC

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Require a dedicated non-default key from a secret provider, fail startup if absent, separate verification from signing, and return only a boolean/attestation status.

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Delete or harden the alternate entry point; centralize bind policy and require explicit deployment configuration validated against authentication mode.

findings.title: Runtime validators can admit nonlocal unsigned development configuration
findings.rootCause: defense_in_depth_root_cause
impact: Programmatic or schema-bypassing configuration could weaken production identity/write-token requirements outside the intended local-development namespace.

evidence.fact: both runtime validators accepted nonlocal tenant/workspace with allowUnsignedLocalDevelopment and no write token
frozen configuration has unsigned development disabled

smallestSafeRepairBoundaries: Enforce local tenant/workspace, loopback URL, nonproduction mode, and explicit warnings directly in runtime validation whenever unsigned development is enabled.
